items.item_text: Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

The Quality Assurance Leader, Aerospace Systems provides technical leadership and independent oversight across the full lifecycle of advanced aerospace systems, from pioneering scientific instruments for interplanetary exploration to next-generation satellite, launch vehicle, and command-and-control architectures. This position ensures quality is engineered into every phase of development by driving rigorous verification, risk management, process discipline, and compliance with NASA Safety & Mission Assurance and aerospace industry standards. Working alongside engineering, manufacturing, integration, and supplier teams, the Quality Assurance Leader, Aerospace Systems helps transform breakthrough concepts into mission-ready hardware capable of performing flawlessly in the unforgiving environments of launch and deep space. Leadership spans design reviews, manufacturing surveillance, hardware inspections, supplier oversight, environmental and functional testing, anomaly resolution, and flight readiness verification, ensuring every system is built for reliability, safety, and mission success. At launch sites, this position provides critical quality oversight during spacecraft integration, fueling, encapsulation, and launch vehicle processing, safeguarding every milestone leading to flight. Through technical excellence, sound judgment, and uncompromising attention to detail, this position helps deliver spacecraft that enable humanity's exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Provides strategic leadership and subject-matter expertise in Aerospace Quality Assurance and NASA Safety & Mission Assurance, setting technical direction and quality standards that drive mission success and enterprise-wide risk mitigation.

Provides expert technical oversight across design, fabrication, integration, and test of spaceflight hardware, evaluating compliance with NASA requirements and flagging quality risks early to protect mission reliability.

Partners with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to resolve complex technical issues, drive effective corrective actions, and build a culture of continuous quality improvement through direct, hands-on technical engagement.

Verifies mission-critical hardware against aerospace quality and workmanship standards through detailed inspections, procedural compliance reviews, manufacturing surveillance, and witnessing of qualification and acceptance testing.

Investigates quality issues, analyzes technical data, and produces clear, actionable reports and documentation that support sound decision-making, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across programs.
Infrequent travel to partners and subcontractors, possible longer travel associated with launches.
Post-graduate level course work in related area (Preferred)
